case.symptom: Itchy red rash on my forearm. Started two days ago after gardening without gloves.

visual_findings: Diffuse erythematous macular and papular eruption across a large skin surface
Linear streaking pattern visible within the rash, suggestive of contact or drag pattern
Scattered discrete erythematous papules interspersed with confluent erythema
No visible vesicles, pustules, or frank urticaria wheal formations at this image resolution
Skin surface appears intact without visible erosions or crusting

possible_causes.name: Allergic Contact Dermatitis
possible_causes.description: Delayed hypersensitivity reaction (Type IV) to plant allergens (e.g., poison ivy/oak/sumac) or other garden substances. The linear streaking pattern is highly characteristic of plant contact dermatitis.

possible_causes.name: Irritant Contact Dermatitis
possible_causes.description: Direct skin irritation from plant sap, thorns, soil chemicals, or fertilizers encountered during gardening without glove protection.

possible_causes.name: Urticaria (Hives)
possible_causes.description: Allergic reaction causing wheals and erythema; could be triggered by insect contact, plant exposure, or topical allergens during gardening.

possible_causes.name: Insect Bite/Sting Reaction
possible_causes.description: Multiple insect bites (e.g., chiggers, caterpillar hair contact) during outdoor activity can produce diffuse papular pruritic eruptions.

possible_causes.name: Phytophotodermatitis
possible_causes.description: Reaction from plant-derived furocoumarins (e.g., wild parsnip, hogweed) activated by UV exposure, producing erythema and potential blistering.

possible_causes.name: Tinea Corporis (Ringworm)
possible_causes.description: Fungal skin infection sometimes acquired via soil contact; typically presents with annular scaling plaques but early presentation can be erythematous.

possible_causes.name: Scabies
possible_causes.description: Mite infestation causing intensely pruritic papular rash; unlikely from gardening alone but possible with certain soil exposure.

red_flags: Rash spreading rapidly to face, neck, or genitals
Development of difficulty breathing, throat tightness, or swelling of lips/tongue (anaphylaxis)
Involvement of eyes causing pain or vision changes
Appearance of large fluid-filled blisters (bullae) or skin sloughing
Fever, chills, or red streaks extending from the rash (possible infection/cellulitis)
Rash involving more than 30% of body surface area or spreading uncontrollably
questions_to_prepare_for: What specific plants or chemicals did you come into contact with while gardening?
Have you had a similar reaction before, or do you have known allergies to plants or latex?
Is the rash spreading beyond the initial area, and have you touched your face or eyes since exposure?
Have you used any topical treatments (creams, antihistamines) since the rash appeared, and did they help?
Did you notice any insect bites, stings, or skin trauma (scratches from thorns) during gardening?
Are you currently taking any medications, including new ones started recently?

possible_causes.name: Contact Dermatitis (Irritant)
possible_causes.description: Skin reaction caused by direct contact with an irritating plant, soil, fertilizer, or gardening chemical without protective gloves.

possible_causes.name: Allergic Contact Dermatitis
possible_causes.description: Immune-mediated allergic reaction to a plant allergen (e.g., poison ivy, poison oak) or other substance encountered during gardening.

possible_causes.name: Poison Ivy / Oak / Sumac (Urushiol Reaction)
possible_causes.description: Delayed hypersensitivity reaction to urushiol oil from toxic plants, typically appearing 12–72 hours after exposure with itchy, streaky red rash.

possible_causes.name: Insect or Mite Bite
possible_causes.description: Bites from insects, chiggers, or mites common in garden environments can cause localized red, itchy welts or rash.

possible_causes.name: Fungal Skin Infection (Tinea)
possible_causes.description: Fungal organisms in soil can infect skin, causing a red, itchy, sometimes ring-shaped rash on exposed areas.

possible_causes.name: Cellulitis
possible_causes.description: Bacterial skin infection that can develop from small cuts or abrasions during gardening; presents as red, warm, swollen skin.

possible_causes.name: Sporotrichosis
possible_causes.description: Fungal infection caused by Sporothrix found in soil and plant matter; can cause nodular lesions following a scratch or puncture wound.

red_flags: Rash spreading rapidly beyond the forearm
Skin becomes hot, swollen, or has red streaking (possible cellulitis or lymphangitis)
Fever, chills, or flu-like symptoms accompanying the rash
Difficulty breathing, throat tightening, or facial swelling (signs of severe allergic reaction)
Blistering or open sores covering large areas of skin
Rash involves the face, eyes, or genitals
questions_to_prepare_for: What plants, chemicals, or materials did you come into contact with while gardening?
Did you notice any scratches, puncture wounds, or insect bites at the time?
Is the rash spreading, staying the same, or improving since it started?
Do you have any known allergies to plants or other substances?
Have you tried any treatments so far (e.g., hydrocortisone cream, antihistamines)?
Do you have any fever or other symptoms beyond the rash?

case.symptom: Something is wrong with my arm. It looks bad.

visual_findings: Diffuse erythematous macular and papular eruption across a large body surface area
Irregular linear and streak-like erythematous patterns interspersed among discrete small papules
Background skin appears mildly flushed with scattered pinpoint red macules
No visible vesicles, bullae, pustules, or open erosions identified
No visible scaling, crusting, or purpuric/non-blanchable lesions discernible at this resolution

possible_causes.name: Urticaria (Hives)
possible_causes.description: The linear, streak-like wheals mixed with scattered papules are highly characteristic of urticaria. Can be triggered by allergens, medications, foods, or infections.

possible_causes.name: Dermatographism
possible_causes.description: The prominent linear marks may represent dermatographism (skin writing), where mechanical pressure causes exaggerated urticarial lines, often occurring alongside a broader reactive rash.

possible_causes.name: Allergic contact dermatitis
possible_causes.description: A delayed hypersensitivity reaction to a substance (lotion, fabric, plant, latex) contacting the skin, producing erythema and papules.

possible_causes.name: Drug reaction / morbilliform exanthem
possible_causes.description: A diffuse erythematous macular-papular rash can be a reaction to a newly started medication, often appearing 7–14 days after initiation.

possible_causes.name: Viral exanthem
possible_causes.description: Many viral infections (e.g., EBV, enteroviruses) produce widespread maculopapular rashes, especially in younger patients.

possible_causes.name: Heat rash (Miliaria rubra)
possible_causes.description: Blocked sweat ducts in hot or humid conditions can produce small erythematous papules over large areas.

possible_causes.name: Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS)
possible_causes.description: A severe, potentially life-threatening drug hypersensitivity with widespread rash and systemic involvement. Rare but serious.

red_flags: Difficulty breathing, throat tightness, or swallowing difficulty (signs of anaphylaxis — call 911 immediately)
Rapid spread of rash to face, lips, or tongue with swelling
High fever (>38.5°C / 101.3°F) accompanying the rash
Rash that does not blanch when pressed (possible purpura/petechiae — seek emergency care)
Mucous membrane involvement (mouth sores, eye redness, genital lesions)
Feeling faint, racing heart, or low blood pressure alongside the rash
questions_to_prepare_for: When did the rash first appear, and has it been spreading or changing in appearance?
Have you started any new medications, supplements, or vitamins in the past 2–4 weeks?
Have you been exposed to any new foods, soaps, lotions, plants, or fabrics recently?
Do you have any associated symptoms such as itching, burning, fever, joint pain, or fatigue?
Do you have any known allergies, and have you had a similar rash before?
Have you been ill recently or had any viral symptoms (sore throat, runny nose, fatigue)?

possible_causes.name: Soft tissue injury or bruising
possible_causes.description: Trauma to the arm can cause visible bruising, swelling, or discoloration from damaged blood vessels under the skin.

possible_causes.name: Fracture or broken bone
possible_causes.description: A broken bone in the arm may cause visible deformity, swelling, bruising, and significant pain.

possible_causes.name: Skin infection or cellulitis
possible_causes.description: A bacterial skin infection can cause redness, warmth, swelling, and visible changes in the appearance of the arm.

possible_causes.name: Allergic reaction or contact dermatitis
possible_causes.description: Exposure to an allergen or irritant can cause rash, hives, redness, or swelling on the arm.

possible_causes.name: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT)
possible_causes.description: A blood clot in a deep vein can cause swelling, redness, warmth, and visible changes to the arm.

possible_causes.name: Abscess or boil
possible_causes.description: A localized collection of pus under the skin can cause a visible, painful lump with redness and swelling.

possible_causes.name: Necrotizing fasciitis
possible_causes.description: A severe, rapidly spreading bacterial infection of the soft tissue that can cause dramatic visible changes and requires emergency treatment.

possible_causes.name: Compartment syndrome
possible_causes.description: Dangerous buildup of pressure within muscle compartments, often after injury, causing severe pain, tightness, and visible swelling.

red_flags: Rapidly spreading redness, swelling, or discoloration
Visible bone or severe deformity
Loss of sensation, movement, or circulation in the arm or hand
Skin that appears black, purple, or has a foul odor (possible tissue death)
Severe, worsening pain that is out of proportion to appearance
Fever, chills, or feeling generally very unwell alongside arm changes
questions_to_prepare_for: When did you first notice something was wrong with your arm, and has it changed since then?
Did you experience any injury, trauma, insect bite, or exposure to something new recently?
Can you describe exactly what it looks like — redness, swelling, bruising, rash, deformity?
Are you experiencing any pain, numbness, tingling, or weakness in the arm?
Do you have any fever, chills, or other symptoms elsewhere in your body?
Do you have any underlying medical conditions such as diabetes, a blood disorder, or a weakened immune system?

case.symptom: Crushing chest pain radiating down my left arm with shortness of breath for the last hour.
case.notes: text describes cardiac emergency, image shows rash

visual_findings: Diffuse erythematous macular and papular rash across the trunk/back
Irregular linear erythematous streaks interspersed among discrete small papules
No visible wheals, vesicles, pustules, or scaling noted
Rash appears widespread and confluent in areas
No obvious petechiae or purpura visible at this image resolution

possible_causes.name: Acute Myocardial Infarction (Heart Attack)
possible_causes.description: Crushing chest pain radiating to the left arm with shortness of breath lasting one hour is a classic presentation of acute MI. THIS IS A MEDICAL EMERGENCY. The skin rash may be incidental or could represent a separate concurrent condition such as an allergic reaction affecting the cardiovascular system (anaphylaxis).

possible_causes.name: Anaphylaxis with cardiac involvement
possible_causes.description: Anaphylaxis can cause urticarial rash, chest pain, and shortness of breath simultaneously. The rash and cardiac symptoms occurring together raises this possibility. Also a medical emergency.

possible_causes.name: Unstable Angina
possible_causes.description: Severe chest pain radiating to the left arm with dyspnea may represent unstable angina, a life-threatening condition requiring immediate evaluation.

possible_causes.name: Aortic Dissection
possible_causes.description: Crushing chest pain can be a presentation of aortic dissection, which is immediately life-threatening.

possible_causes.name: Pulmonary Embolism
possible_causes.description: Chest pain and shortness of breath can indicate a pulmonary embolism, especially if accompanied by other risk factors.

possible_causes.name: Urticaria / Allergic Reaction (rash only)
possible_causes.description: The visible rash pattern is consistent with urticaria or a viral exanthem, but this does NOT explain the cardiac symptoms described.

red_flags: ⚠️ STOP — Call 911 (or your local emergency number) IMMEDIATELY. Do NOT wait for a doctor's appointment.
Crushing chest pain lasting over one hour is a cardiac emergency
Left arm radiation of chest pain is a classic heart attack warning sign
Shortness of breath combined with chest pain requires emergency evaluation
If rash and chest/breathing symptoms are concurrent, anaphylaxis must be ruled out emergently
Do not drive yourself — call emergency services now
questions_to_prepare_for: When exactly did the chest pain start and has it changed in intensity?
Do you have a history of heart disease, high blood pressure, or high cholesterol?
Did you take any new medications, foods, or have any known allergen exposures before symptoms started?
Do you have any other symptoms such as nausea, sweating, dizziness, or palpitations?
Have you had this rash before, and when did it appear relative to the chest pain?
Do you smoke, and what is your family history of heart disease?

possible_causes.name: Acute Myocardial Infarction (Heart Attack)
possible_causes.description: Blockage of coronary artery causing heart muscle damage. Classic presentation includes crushing chest pain radiating to left arm with shortness of breath.

possible_causes.name: Unstable Angina
possible_causes.description: Severe reduction in blood flow to the heart without complete blockage. Symptoms mirror a heart attack and require urgent evaluation.

possible_causes.name: Aortic Dissection
possible_causes.description: Tearing of the aorta's inner layer, causing severe chest pain that can radiate to the arm. A life-threatening emergency.

possible_causes.name: Pulmonary Embolism
possible_causes.description: Blood clot in the lungs causing chest pain and shortness of breath. Can present similarly to cardiac events.

possible_causes.name: Musculoskeletal Chest Pain
possible_causes.description: Costochondritis or muscle strain causing chest pain. However, radiation to the left arm makes this less likely.

possible_causes.name: Severe GERD or Esophageal Spasm
possible_causes.description: Esophageal conditions can mimic cardiac pain but rarely cause left arm radiation or significant shortness of breath.

red_flags: Crushing or pressure-like chest pain lasting more than a few minutes — call 911 immediately
Pain radiating to the left arm, jaw, neck, or back
Shortness of breath accompanying chest pain
Sweating, nausea, or lightheadedness alongside chest pain
Symptoms persisting for one hour without relief
Any loss of consciousness or near-fainting
questions_to_prepare_for: When exactly did the pain start and has it been constant or come and go?
On a scale of 1–10, how severe is the pain, and has it changed in intensity?
Do you have a history of heart disease, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, or diabetes?
Are you experiencing any sweating, nausea, dizziness, or palpitations?
Do you smoke, and what medications are you currently taking?
Have you had episodes like this before, and if so, were you given a diagnosis?
